grade_reason: His one 2026 remark on AI risk asks whether the AI race might be engineering our own destruction; because it is phrased as a question to the panel rather than his stated view, it is graded C (boundary with A).
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. The 16 April 2026 quote was read through a page-fetch tool that would not reproduce whole paragraphs; the short phrase was returned identically from two copies of the AP story (min.house.gov and theoutpost.ai), and the CTV News copy showed no body text. A reviewer should confirm the exact wording and punctuation in the original AP story; the AP paraphrase around it says he asked whether anyone on the panel believed this 'amid the AI race'. A reviewer could reasonably grade it A under ruling 1 (threat to our survival) if the question is read as endorsing the concern. No sign he sponsored or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (the Casar press release names only Casar and Sanders). His press release page (crane.house.gov/media) lists no AI releases among the 10 most recent; crane.house.gov/media/press-releases returned 404. The September 2025 hearing also had him ask what AI regulations witnesses would consider responsible and how to balance AI use in schools; these are D and left out.
